What Is Schnitz?

Schnitz is an Australian fast-casual chain that does one thing really well: fresh, hand-crumbed schnitzels. The first store opened in Melbourne in 2002, and the brand has since grown to dozens of locations across Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia and beyond.

Every schnitzel is crumbed in store and cooked to order. You can choose chicken, beef or a plant-based schnitzel, pick a crumb or a crumb-free flavour, and have it as a burger, a wrap, a salad or a plate with chips. That mix-and-match approach is why the menu can feel huge the first time you visit – and why a clear guide like this one is handy.

SchnitzMenu.com is an independent fan guide. We collect prices from public sources, store listings and delivery apps, mark every price as approximate, and refresh the data every month.

Schnitz Menu 2026 – Full Menu with Prices & Calories (Australia)

Every item on the Schnitz menu in one place: wraps and burgers, schnitzel plates, salads, tenders, kids meals, chips and drinks. Updated monthly. Unofficial guide – not affiliated with Schnitz International.

Looking at the Schnitz menu for the first time can be a little overwhelming. You pick a protein, a crumb or flavour, then decide whether you want it in a burger, a wrap, on a plate or on a salad. This guide lays the whole menu out category by category, with an approximate Australian price and calorie count wherever one is publicly available.

Use the search box to find an item fast, tap a column heading to sort by price or calories, or press + next to any item to build a meal and see the running total. Prices are typical pickup prices – delivery apps usually charge more, and some stores (airports, stadiums, CBD food courts) price higher again.

[sm_jump_nav] [sm_menu_search] [sm_print]

How to Order at Schnitz

  1. Choose your schnitzel. Chicken is the classic. Beef and plant-based schnitzels are available in most wraps and burgers.
  2. Pick a crumb or flavour. Traditional crumbs, spicy crumbs, a buttermilk breader, or a crumb-free flavour such as lemon pepper or Moroccan spices.
  3. Pick a format. Burger, wrap, plate with chips, or salad.
  4. Add sides and a drink. Chips, sweet potato chips, slaw, dips and soft drinks.

Schnitz Calories – Highest Calorie Items

If you are watching your energy intake, the plates with chips are the big ones. A loaded schnitzel with chips can pass 1,000 calories on its own. Calorie figures below come from third-party nutrition databases and should be treated as estimates.

Schnitz Allergen Information

The chicken itself is listed with no allergens – it is the coating that matters. Traditional crumbs contain wheat, gluten, egg, milk, soy and sesame. See the full matrix before you order if you have a food allergy.

Open the allergen guide

About Schnitz in Australia

Schnitz started in Melbourne in 2002 with a simple idea: take the pub schnitzel, crumb it fresh in front of the customer, and serve it fast. More than twenty years later the chain has stores in shopping centres, high streets and food courts across several states.

What makes Schnitz different from other fast food chains is the cooking method. Schnitzels are crumbed by hand during service rather than arriving pre-crumbed and frozen, which is why the queue moves a little slower at lunch – and why fans think it is worth the wait.

The menu changes regularly with limited-time burgers, seasonal specials and family bundles. We check prices and new items at the start of every month and update this page.

Approximate Australian prices for every Schnitz wrap, burger, plate, tender, kids meal and side. Sort by price, search the list and build a meal to see your total.

How much does Schnitz cost? In most Australian stores a schnitzel wrap or burger sits between about $14 and $17 (approx.), while a schnitzel plate with chips costs roughly $19.50 to $25.50 (approx.). Kids meals start around $11 (approx.) and a dip is about $2 (approx.).

The prices below are typical pickup prices collected from public sources and store listings. They change between states and stores, and delivery apps such as Uber Eats and DoorDash usually add a mark-up. Where we could not confirm a price, the table says Varies rather than guessing.

  • Deals. App-only and limited-time bundles can be much cheaper than ordering items separately.

Tip: if you are feeding a family, compare the bundle price against ordering items one by one using the meal builder on this page.

The cheapest things you can buy at Schnitz are a dipping sauce (about $2 approx.) and a small serve of tenders (about $7.90 approx.). For a full meal on a budget, look out for value deals that bundle a small wrap, mini chips and a drink, which have sold for around $10 in the past.

Schnitz Calories & Nutrition Guide 2026 (Australia)

How many calories are in a Schnitz schnitzel? Calorie and kilojoule counts for popular Schnitz items, a top-10 chart and tips for a lighter order.

Schnitz meals are hearty. A classic Schnitzel & Chips comes in at roughly 779 calories (3,259 kJ), a Parma & Chips at about 897 calories, and a Loaded Schnitzel & Chips can reach around 1,150 calories. For comparison, the average Australian adult daily intake used on food labels is 8,700 kJ (about 2,080 calories).

The figures on this page come from third-party nutrition databases and public sources. They are estimates – serving sizes, crumbs and sauces change the numbers. Where we do not have a reliable figure we leave it blank instead of guessing.

Schnitz Calorie Chart – Top Items

[sm_calorie_chart top='10']

Schnitz Nutrition Table (Calories & Kilojoules)

Tap a column heading to sort. Kilojoules are calculated from calories (1 kcal = 4.184 kJ).

[sm_nutrition_table]

How to Order a Lighter Meal at Schnitz

  • Swap chips for salad. Chips add several hundred calories to any plate.
  • Go for a salad with schnitzel. You still get the schnitzel without the bun or wrap.
  • Try a crumb-free flavour. Lemon pepper or Moroccan spices skip the crumb coating.
  • Watch the sauces. Creamy mayo and aioli add up quickly. Ask for sauce on the side.
  • Share the tenders. One original tender is about 152 calories.
  • Choose water. A 600ml soft drink can add around 250 calories.

Which Schnitz Item Has the Most Calories?

Based on available data, the Loaded Schnitzel & Chips is the highest-calorie single item at around 1,150 calories (approx.). Large tender packs meant for sharing will be higher in total, but they are designed to split between two or more people.

Schnitz Allergen Menu 2026 – Gluten, Egg, Milk, Soy & Sesame

A clear allergen guide for the Schnitz menu in Australia, organised by crumb and coating. Always confirm with your local store before ordering.

Important: this guide summarises publicly available allergen information to help you plan. It is not medical advice. Schnitz kitchens handle wheat, egg, milk, soy and sesame, so cross-contact is possible. If you have a serious allergy or coeliac disease, speak to the staff and check the official allergen chart before you order.

The key thing to understand about Schnitz allergens is that the protein itself (plain chicken) is listed with no allergens. Most allergens come from the crumb, the breader and the sauces. Choosing a different coating changes what you are eating.

Schnitz Allergen Matrix by Crumb

[sm_allergens]

Is Schnitz Gluten Free?

Traditional crumbed schnitzels are not gluten free – the flour, egg wash and breadcrumbs all contain gluten. Even the crumb-free lemon pepper flavour is listed as containing gluten. Schnitz does list a gluten free wrap on its allergen chart, but because gluten is everywhere in the kitchen, people with coeliac disease should ask staff how it is prepared before ordering.

In Australia a product can only be labelled gluten free if it contains no detectable gluten under the Food Standards Code, which is a very high bar for a busy fast food kitchen.

Schnitz Egg, Milk, Soy and Sesame Allergies

  • Egg: used in traditional crumbing. Ask about crumb-free options.
  • Milk: present in traditional crumbs, the buttermilk breader, cheese and many sauces.
  • Soy: listed in traditional crumbs and some sauces.
  • Sesame: listed in traditional crumbs and often in burger buns.

Plant-Based and Vegan Options

Schnitz offers a plant-based schnitzel in many burgers and wraps. Plant-based does not always mean vegan or allergen free: crumbs, buns and sauces may contain egg or milk. Check the official chart for the exact combination you want.

What is on the Schnitz kids menu, how much it costs and what comes in each pack.

The Schnitz kids menu, called Little Rascals, was refreshed with two main options: the Kiddy Schnugget Pack and the Teeny Weeny. Both come as a complete meal with mini chips and a drink, which makes them an easy choice for younger eaters.

About SchnitzMenu.com

Who runs this site, why it exists and how we keep the information accurate.

Why We Built This Guide

SchnitzMenu.com is an independent, unofficial guide to the Schnitz menu in Australia. We built it because finding simple answers – how much a parma costs, how many calories are in a wrap, which crumbs contain egg – meant digging through delivery apps, PDFs and old forum posts. We wanted one clear, fast page that answered those questions properly.

Who We Are

The site is run by RK Mohsin, a website publisher focused on helpful, easy-to-read food guides. We are fans of the food, not employees of the company. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Schnitz International Pty Ltd.

How We Collect and Check Prices

  • We gather prices from public sources, store listings and delivery apps.
  • Every price is marked (approx.) because prices vary between stores, states and ordering methods.
  • Where we cannot confirm a price or calorie figure, we say so instead of guessing.
  • We review the data at the start of every month and update the date shown on each page.

Corrections

Spotted a price that has changed or a new menu item? Please let us know through the contact page and we will update the guide.

How This Site Is Funded

SchnitzMenu.com is free to use. We may earn money from advertising (such as Google AdSense) and from affiliate links to food delivery services. This never changes the prices or information we publish.

Privacy Policy

How SchnitzMenu.com collects, uses and protects your information.

Overview

This policy explains how SchnitzMenu.com (we, us) handles personal information. We follow the Australian Privacy Principles in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). By using this site you agree to this policy.

Information We Collect

  • Information you give us – such as your name and email when you contact us or subscribe to updates.
  • Usage information – pages visited, device and browser type, and approximate location, collected through cookies and analytics tools such as Google Analytics.

Cookies and Advertising

We use cookies to understand how the site is used and to show advertising. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your previous visits to this and other websites. Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads based on your visits to this site and/or other sites on the internet.

You can opt out of personalised advertising by visiting Google Ads Settings or aboutads.info. You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings.

Affiliate Links

Some links to food delivery services are affiliate links. If you order through them we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. These services have their own privacy policies.

How We Use Information

  • To reply to your messages.
  • To improve the site and its content.
  • To show relevant advertising.
  • To meet legal obligations.

We do not sell your personal information.

Access, Correction and Complaints

You can ask to access or correct the personal information we hold about you by emailing hello@schnitzmenu.com. If you are unhappy with how we handled your information you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC).

Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version is always on this page.
